text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Security forces kill 20 "terrorists" after they ambushed a convoy carrying medicines in western Algeria. The forces killed the assailants in Saida province last week after the ambush in which four civilians were killed.
- A home-made bomb exploded in a train early on Saturday killing one passenger and wounding three. The train was travelling between El Affroun, west of Algiers, to the capital.
- The authorities end de facto monopoly of state-owned banking system. The Credit and Money Council grants licence to a second private bank.
- Twenty-one party leaders, who met President Liamine Zeroual's senior aide, urged the authorities to delay local elections planned for early October and amend the election law.
- A bomb explosion wounds five passengers on the train linking El Affroun to Algiers on Saturday.
- Gunmen on Thursday shot dead a camerawoman, Louisa Ait Adda, working for the state-owned Audivisual Production National Office in central Algiers.
